Error state

What a view shows when its data could not be loaded, with a way to try again.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • In place of a list, table, panel or whole view whose data failed to load.
  • When the reader can do something about it, at least trying again.

When not to use it

  • When the view loaded and one action in it failed. Use an alert beside that action.
  • For a mistake in a form control. Use the field's error message.
  • When the view loaded and has nothing in it. Use an empty state.

Accessibility

  • Set role="alert" on the error state when it replaces content after a failed load, so a screen reader announces it. Leave the role off while a retry is running, so the same failure is not announced twice.
  • The title is a heading at the level that fits the view's outline, and says what failed in the reader's terms: The runs could not be loaded.
  • The sentence after the title is a plain paragraph with no class. It says what to do next. Never show only a status code or a stack trace.
  • The Retry action is a gw-button inside gw-error-state__action. While it runs, set aria-busy="true" on it and change its label to Retrying.
  • Technical detail goes in a native details element with a text summary, closed by default. Enter or Space on the summary opens and closes it.
  • The detail is plain text in a pre element, so it can be selected and copied into a bug report. Long lines wrap.
  • The icon beside the title is drawn by the stylesheet and needs no markup.
